title: Sodium Metal in Water – Vigorous Reaction Lab
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D chemistry lab simulation of dropping sodium metal into water using Three.js and GLTFLoader. The scene simulates the vigorous exothermic reaction Na + H₂O → NaOH + ½H₂ with dynamic difficulty scaling.

SCENE SETUP:
- Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 5, 10) looking at origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light from (5, 10, 5) intensity 0.8.
- Create a transparent glass beaker (cylinder geometry, radius 2, height 4, open top) centered at origin. Use MeshPhysicalMaterial with transmission=0.9, roughness=0.05, transparent=true, opacity=0.3.
- Fill the beaker with water represented by a blue semi-transparent plane/box (MeshStandardMaterial, color #2244aa, opacity 0.5) at y=1 inside the beaker.
- Load the asset 'Lantern.glb' using GLTFLoader and place it on a shelf/table to the right of the beaker at position (5, 0, 0) scaled to (0.5, 0.5, 0.5). It serves as the lab's ambient lantern providing warm point light (color #ffaa44, intensity 0.6) from its position.
- Create a sodium metal chunk as a small silver-grey sphere (radius 0.3) initially positioned above the beaker at (0, 6, 0), not yet dropped.
- Add an OrbitControls for camera rotation.

PHYSICS & CHEMISTRY SIMULATION:
- When sodium is dropped, it falls under gravity (9.81 m/s²) until it hits the water surface (y=1).
- Upon contact with water, the reaction begins. Track elapsed reaction time in seconds.
- Reaction produces: hydrogen gas (H₂ bubbles), heat (temperature rise), and NaOH (pH increase).
- BUBBLES: Spawn bubble particles (small white spheres) rising from the sodium chunk. Bubble rate = baseBubbleRate * difficultyMultiplier. baseBubbleRate = 5 bubbles/sec. Bubbles rise at 1.5 units/sec and pop (are removed) when they reach y=3.5 or after 2 seconds.
- TEMPERATURE: Starts at 20°C. Rises by 0.8°C/sec * difficultyMultiplier during active reaction. Max temperature = 100°C. After reaction ends, cools at 0.3°C/sec back toward 20°C.
- pH: Starts at 7.0 (neutral). Increases by 0.5/sec * difficultyMultiplier during reaction toward max 14.0. pH never exceeds 14.0 or drops below 0.
- SODIUM MASS: Starts at 1.0 unit. Consumed at rate 0.1/sec * difficultyMultiplier. Reaction ends when mass <= 0. Sodium chunk visually shrinks (scale proportional to remaining mass). When mass reaches 0, remove the sodium mesh.
- HYDROGEN PRODUCED: Tracks total H₂ moles produced. For every 0.1 mass consumed, 0.05 moles H₂ produced. Conservation law: totalH2Produced must equal (1.0 - currentSodiumMass) * 0.5 at all times (within epsilon 0.001).
- Water color shifts from blue (#2244aa) toward purple/pink (#aa22aa) as pH rises above 10 (phenolphthalein indicator simulation). Interpolate linearly between pH 7-14.

DYNAMIC DIFFICULTY:
- difficultyLevel: integer 1-5, starts at 1.
- difficultyMultiplier = difficultyLevel (so level 1 = 1x, level 5 = 5x speed).
- Keyboard 'ArrowUp' increases difficulty by 1 (max 5). 'ArrowDown' decreases by 1 (min 1).
- Difficulty changes take effect immediately on all rates.

USER INTERACTIONS:
- SPACEBAR: Drop the sodium into the water (only works once, before reaction starts). Sets reactionStarted=true.
- 'R' key: Reset/Undo the entire experiment. Sodium reappears at (0,6,0) full size, temperature=20, pH=7, H₂=0, all bubbles removed, water color reset, reactionStarted=false, reactionComplete=false. Difficulty level is preserved.
- 'P' key: Pause/unpause the simulation. Toggles paused state.
- Mouse click on the lantern model: Toggle lantern light on/off (toggles the point light enabled state and tracks lanternOn boolean).
- DOM button '#btn-emergency-stop': Immediately halts the reaction (sets reactionComplete=true, stops all bubble generation, stops temperature/pH changes, freezes sodium mass at current value).

HUD / UI:
- Top-left overlay div showing: Temperature (°C, 1 decimal), pH (1 decimal), Sodium Mass (2 decimals), H₂ Produced (3 decimals), Difficulty Level, Paused status, Reaction status (idle/active/complete).
- A red button with id='btn-emergency-stop' labeled 'EMERGENCY STOP' at bottom-center.
- A small status bar showing difficulty as colored pips (green=1 to red=5).

STATE MANAGEMENT (window.__3D_STATE__):
Expose and continuously update:
- temperature: number (°C)
- pH: number
- sodiumMass: number (0 to 1)
- hydrogenProduced: number (moles)
- difficultyLevel: number (1-5)
- difficultyMultiplier: number
- reactionStarted: boolean
- reactionComplete: boolean
- paused: boolean
- lanternOn: boolean
- lanternLoaded: boolean (true once Lantern.glb is loaded)
- bubbleCount: number (current active bubbles in scene)
- waterColorHex: string (current water material color as hex)
- sodiumPosition: {x, y, z}
- elapsedReactionTime: number (seconds since reaction started, 0 if not started)
- conservationError: number (absolute difference between hydrogenProduced and (1-sodiumMass)*0.5)
- resetCount: number (how many times R was pressed)
- emergencyStopUsed: boolean
physics_constraints: Gravity 9.81 m/s² for sodium drop. Conservation law: hydrogenProduced === (1.0 - sodiumMass) * 0.5 within epsilon 0.001 at all times. Temperature bounded [20, 100]°C. pH bounded [0, 14]. Sodium mass bounded [0, 1]. Bubble positions bounded within beaker radius and y∈[1, 3.5]. Reaction rates scale linearly with difficultyMultiplier. Energy/mass conservation must hold through pause/unpause and difficulty changes.
